subject: cognitive-science
intro: Cognitive science leads to work on how minds and machines process information — user research and human factors, clinical psychology and neuropsychology, data science and the labs that model thought itself.

roles.title: Data Scientists
roles.what: Extract knowledge from data: build models and algorithms, run statistical analyses on large datasets, design experiments, and turn patterns into predictions and decisions for organisations.
roles.where: Unit 7's Bayesian models of cognition and symbolic-versus-connectionist modelling, plus unit 5's judgment-under-uncertainty topics, train the statistical reasoning and model design this role sells.

roles.title: Human Factors Engineers and Ergonomists
roles.what: Design technology around human limits: study how people perceive, attend and act while using systems, test prototypes, and redesign cockpits, software and workstations so they are safer, faster and less error-prone.
roles.where: Unit 2's perception and illusions, unit 3's attention limits, and unit 8's cognitive ergonomics and HCI topics are exactly the research base this profession applies to systems design.

roles.title: Clinical and Counseling Psychologists
roles.what: Assess and treat mental health problems: test and interview clients, diagnose disorders, deliver psychological treatments, and track outcomes — combining clinical judgement with research evidence.
roles.where: Unit 3's memory errors and false memories, unit 8's mental health and cognition topics, and the cognitive neuroscience methods of unit 6 ground the assessment work this role does.

roles.title: Neuropsychologists
roles.what: Evaluate how brain conditions change thinking: administer batteries that test memory, language and executive function, diagnose disorders of higher cerebral functioning, and plan rehabilitation after injury or illness.
roles.where: Unit 6 — fMRI, EEG and lesion-study methods, functional brain systems, consciousness studies — is the direct training ground for relating test performance to damaged or developing brain systems.

roles.title: Psychology Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach psychology and cognitive science at universities: lecture on perception, memory, development and research methods, run lab courses, supervise thesis students, and publish empirical research.
roles.where: This course's interdisciplinary arc — philosophy of mind through perception, memory, language, neuroscience and computation — is the undergraduate curriculum such teachers design and deliver.
